messages:
anya: heads up 1: rerank-v4 int4 bringup on shadowbench showing ndcg@10 +0.4% but MRR down ~7% on golden-queries slice. anyone seen this pattern with int4?
mika: int4 can exaggerate rounding at the head. did we keep the exact same golden query set between baseline and candidate?
david: i compared the hashes; the set is identical but distribution of top1 candidates changed for ~120 of the 2k gold queries.
mika: interesting. any preprocessing changes recently? html-strip or title->snippet mapping?
david: there was a small ingest tweak that preserves <strong> tags in snippet field to keep emphasis. maybe tokenization changed.
anya: that could do it. emphasis tags change token boundaries and attention for short docs. run a subset stripping html and see effect.
mika: i'll run a quick parity eval: baseline(fp16)-v4 vs candidate(int4)-v4, both with html-stripped and html-preserved.
eval-bot: quick parity summary (N=2000 gold queries):
  - baseline(fp16, html-stripped): ndcg@10=0.481, mrr=0.332
  - candidate(int4, html-preserved): ndcg@10=0.484, mrr=0.309
  - candidate(int4, html-stripped): ndcg@10=0.483, mrr=0.328
david: stripping html during eval recovers most of the MRR. suggests the quant calibration didn't see emphasized tokens.
anya: two actionable items: 1) augment PTQ calibration corpus with html-preserved examples, 2) add a golden-query parity check to onboarding that toggles html-strip vs preserve and fails if top1 delta > 1% for golds.
mika: also propose a microfix: canonicalize snippets in the candidate pipeline for canary (strip tags) until recalibration completes. low-risk.
david: i'll open a tiny ops ticket to canonicalize for canary and add the parity check in the eval harness. ticket: INF-8420.
eval-bot: scheduling calibration job with augmented corpus: job-id calibrate-185555-A queued.
anya: perfect. also add a note to the bringup doc: "int4 quant is sensitive to tokenization-emphasis artifacts (html/markup). always mirror prod ingest in calibration corpus."
mika: adding to the runbook and will follow up with results tomorrow. :+1:
